subject.title: Add comprehensive AWS deployment guide (EC2, ECS, Lambda)

question: Which AWS deployment paths and exposure/security defaults should OpenClaw officially document for EC2/Lightsail, ECS/Fargate, and Lambda applicability?
rationale: The guide would become public production advice for gateway exposure, authentication, IAM/task roles, secret storage, persistent state, backups, and serverless support, so automation should not choose those defaults without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Dedicated AWS Guide With Security Review
options.body: Document EC2/Lightsail Docker Compose first, add ECS/Fargate persistence and task-role guidance, state Lambda support limits, and review the external sample before linking it.

options.title: Link External Sample Only
options.body: Add a short pointer to the AWS sample repository while leaving OpenClaw-specific topology and security defaults mostly undocumented.

options.title: Defer AWS Guidance
options.body: Keep relying on generic VPS, Docker, Kubernetes, Gateway, and Bedrock docs until maintainers are ready to own AWS production guidance.

recommendation.title: Dedicated AWS Guide With Security Review
recommendation.body: Document EC2/Lightsail Docker Compose first, add ECS/Fargate persistence and task-role guidance, state Lambda support limits, and review the external sample before linking it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already supplied the concrete keep-open plan and security-review direction in the issue discussion, and recent docs history shows broad docs ownership signal.
